key_insight: Foundation ML interatomic potentials can reproduce simple geometric ordering in correlated perovskites, but they struggle as the target order becomes more local and electronically complex.
engineering_relevance: This work shows where off-the-shelf ML potentials are reliable for fast perovskite simulations and where domain-specific training or electronic-structure methods are still needed.
method: Ran 1 ns molecular dynamics on 80- and 160-atom supercells
Tested three foundation MLIPs with no system-specific training
Compared predictions across 50–300 K for LaMnO3, LaCoO3, and NdNiO3
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated low-temperature bond, orbital, and spin order in three isostructural ABO3 oxides and found a clear hierarchy of success: NdNiO3 is captured, LaMnO3 is only partially captured, and LaCoO3 remains inaccessible.
watch_item: Current foundation MLIPs may miss on-site spin-state transitions and symmetry-sensitive orbital ordering, so they should not be used alone for strongly correlated oxides.
paper_title: Bond, orbital and spin order in d4/d6/d7 perovskite oxides: successes and limitations of foundation interatomic potentials
